g11-geography-ug6-t1.overview: Persistent Environmental Changes sits inside Major Global Environmental Changes. Environmental changes are the focus of Unit 6 of Grade 11 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it examines persistent environmental changes, from habitat loss and farming intensification to overexploitation and invasive species. Then it traces the poverty-environment nexus, linking land degradation and deforestation to hardship, and it presents sustainable development as the answer, pointing ahead to Unit 7: Geographic Issues and Public Concerns. Students will also learn how environmental changes apply to real-life situations.
objectives: Describe the persistent environmental changes that reshape ecosystems.
Explain how habitat loss and farming intensification cut biodiversity.
Distinguish the four phases of an invasive species invasion.
Analyse the poverty-environment nexus for land degradation and deforestation.
Identify the types, causes, and effects of environmental degradation.
g11-geography-ug6-t1.simple:
Persistent Environmental Changes in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, habitat destruction and the extinction debt it leaves behind.
  • How farming intensification lifts yields yet drains soil and biodiversity.
  • Then overexploitation through overfishing, overgrazing, over-logging, and over-drafting.
  • Finally, invasive species such as water hyacinth on Lake Tana.
